channel.title: Communications Earth & Environment
channel.description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

item.title: Government support drives agroforestry adoption and tree cultivation in smallholder farming systems
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04098-3

Participation in government-supported agroforestry programs increases commercial tree cultivation in Madhya Pradesh, whereas awareness alone has little effect, based on surveys of 870 farm households across 59 villages integrated with geospatial data.
item.dc:title: Government support drives agroforestry adoption and tree cultivation in smallholder farming systems

item.title: Anthropogenic warming is projected to divert atmospheric rivers toward densely populated Asia
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04075-w

Thermodynamic enhancement of atmospheric rivers (ARs) is projected to dominate subtropical and midlatitude regions, resulting in increased extreme precipitation in Asian urban areas, according to a study integrating a large ensemble of high-resolution global climate models for AR projections.
item.dc:title: Anthropogenic warming is projected to divert atmospheric rivers toward densely populated Asia

item.title: Groundwater regulates the spatial pattern of photosynthesis in the contiguous United States
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 26 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04067-w

Groundwater, represented by water table depth, plays a critical role in shaping spatial patterns of photosynthesis across the United States, with effects comparable to aridity, according to a study that integrates satellite solar-induced fluorescence, water table depth estimates, and explainable machine learning.
item.dc:title: Groundwater regulates the spatial pattern of photosynthesis in the contiguous United States

item.title: Incorporating landscape context into species distribution models improves predictions for migratory shorebirds
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04094-7

Incorporating landscape-context variables can improve habitat predictions for migratory shorebirds, based on landscape-scale species distribution models of six species in the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.
item.dc:title: Incorporating landscape context into species distribution models improves predictions for migratory shorebirds

item.title: China’s changing diets improve human health but increase environmental pressures
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04063-0

China’s dietary transitions improve health outcomes but increase environmental pressures, with faster health gains but rising environmental impacts in urban areas and slower health gains yet higher environmental burdens in rural areas, according to analysis combining environmental and health indicators and scenario modeling
item.dc:title: China’s changing diets improve human health but increase environmental pressures

item.title: Social structural factors outperform economic assumptions in explaining global municipal waste generation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04059-w

The Human Development Index, CO2 emissions per capita, disease prevalence, and life expectancy are key predictors of municipal waste generation across countries, according to a machine learning analysis of 239 indicators from 195 countries.
item.dc:title: Social structural factors outperform economic assumptions in explaining global municipal waste generation

item.title: Limited impact of the 2025 Kamchatka tsunami explained by the complex seismic rupture
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04050-5

A joint inversion of sea-surface and satellite data suggests the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake exhibited only limited shallow slip and seafloor deformation which explains the suppressed far-field amplitudes despite substantial local run-up.
item.dc:title: Limited impact of the 2025 Kamchatka tsunami explained by the complex seismic rupture

item.title: Land use sequestration potential and uncertainties in India’s net-zero pathway
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04035-4

Land use in India could remove 68–719 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually by 2070, with forests and tree cover sequestering 8.8–12.4 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent during 2015–2070, according to an integrated economic, soil and vegetation carbon assessment.
item.dc:title: Land use sequestration potential and uncertainties in India’s net-zero pathway
